match.reason: The bank point covers true bearings as three-figure angles but does not teach the 16-point compass (NNE, WSW and so on), which the new point requires, so it is a narrower match and a new point is safer.

draft.title: The 16-point compass and bearings
card: The 4 main compass points are north, east, south and west. Adding north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west gives 8 points.
The 16-point compass splits the gaps again. It adds names such as NNE (north-north-east) and WSW (west-south-west). Each name is the two nearest points, with the closer main point said first.
A bearing gives a direction as an angle from 0 to 360 degrees. It is measured clockwise from north, so north is 0, east is 90, south is 180 and west is 270.

A bearing is usually written with three figures, such as 045 degrees for north-east. To find one on a map, put the centre of a protractor on the start point, line it up with north, and read the angle clockwise to the place you want.
draft.remember: A bearing is an angle from 0 to 360 degrees, measured clockwise from north.

a.q: A hiker walks due east. What is the bearing of her direction?
a.why: Bearings start at north (0) and turn clockwise, and east is a quarter of a full turn, so 90 degrees. 270 degrees is west, which comes from turning the wrong way.
a.clue: Turn clockwise from north by a quarter of a full circle.

b.q: Mia stands at the lookout in Katoomba and sees a waterfall on a bearing of 225 degrees. In which direction is the waterfall?
b.why: 225 is halfway between south (180) and west (270), so the waterfall is to the south-west. North-west is 315 degrees, which is a tempting guess if the angle is wrongly measured anticlockwise from north.
b.clue: Find which two main points 225 lies between.

wants.brief: A compass rose with a circle marked in degrees. North is labelled 0, east 90, south 180 and west 270. A curved arrow runs clockwise from north to show the direction of measurement. The 16 compass points are marked around the circle, including NNE and WSW.
wants.why: It shows the 16 points and how bearings are measured clockwise from north in one view.

problems.detail: The why says north-west (315 degrees) is what you get if 225 is wrongly measured anticlockwise from north. Measuring 225 degrees anticlockwise from north actually lands on south-east, not north-west. The explanation of the distractor is wrong and should be rewritten, for example pointing to south-east as the anticlockwise error.

check.summary: Both questions have correct answers (090 degrees and south-west). The why for question b wrongly says an anticlockwise error gives north-west, when it actually gives south-east.
